bull_argument.argument:
TSM is the single most defensible position in the entire AI compute stack, and the market is currently paying an unremarkable price for it. Forward P/E of 19.0x against guided FY2026 revenue growth of slightly above +40% in USD terms is a sub-0.5x PEG on a company earning 50.8% operating margins from a capital-intensive manufacturer. July 2026 revenue of NT$467.58bn (+44.7% YoY) is a record, and it is the run-rate expression of a $60-64bn capex program with 70-80% directed at advanced nodes, three new 3nm fabs coming online across Taiwan, Arizona and Kumamoto, and NT$992bn of free cash flow funding all of it against debt of just 0.63x annual net income and 19.9% debt/equity. This is a monopoly-economics business self-funding a generational capacity expansion, not a cyclical levering into a top.

The two loudest bear objections are valuation and margin dilution, and both are weaker than they look. On margins: the guided 2-4pp gross margin dilution from overseas fabs was the central 2025 bear thesis, and the data has already begun refuting it — Arizona generated NT$36.1bn of profit in H1 2026 alone versus NT$16.1bn for all of 2025, roughly 4.5x the prior full-year run rate, which means the dilution is landing at the mild end of guidance or better. On valuation, the trailing 31.2x versus a 22.8x historical median is exactly what you expect when earnings are inflecting faster than price; the forward 19.0x is the number that matters, and it sits below the historical median while growth is at a multi-year high. GuruFocus's $326.37 GF Value flag is anchored to historical growth and margin regimes, which is precisely what a 44.7% revenue print and a 97/100 quality score say has changed. Meanwhile 18 of 19 analysts are buy-or-better with zero sells for four straight months and a $542.64 street target implying ~31% upside.

The honest risks are geopolitical and macro-technical, not fundamental. Cross-strait tail risk is genuinely unpriceable, but it is also the reason the multiple is 19x instead of 30x, and TSMC is actively de-risking it via the Arizona and Kumamoto build-out. The January 2026 US-Taiwan trade agreement converts that geographic diversification into a competitive moat: reduced or fully excluded Section 232 semiconductor tariffs for chipmakers expanding US production. FX is a live tailwind with USD/TWD at ~31.94 and TWD still ~6% weaker YoY on largely USD-denominated sales. On the technicals, the 08-18 rejection at SMA-50 (424.79) down to 413.41 is a 4.1% pullback within a structure still +86.9% off the 52-week low and comfortably above a 363.53 SMA-200 — an entry point, not a trend break.
key_points: Valuation is the bull case, not the risk: 19.0x forward P/E is below the 22.8x historical median while revenue growth runs above +40% and operating margins hold at 50.8%.
The central bear thesis is already breaking: Arizona earned NT$36.1bn in H1 2026 versus NT$16.1bn for all of 2025, evidence the guided 2-4pp dilution is landing at the mild end or better.
Growth is funded from internal cash, not leverage: NT$992bn FCF supports $60-64bn capex against 19.9% debt/equity and debt at 0.63x annual net income.
Geographic diversification has become a tariff moat: the Jan 2026 US-Taiwan agreement grants reduced or excluded Section 232 tariffs to chipmakers expanding US production.
The setup favors entry: the 4.1% break to 413.41 sits above SMA-200 (363.53) within a +86.9% uptrend, against a $542.64 street target (~31% upside) with zero sells for four months.

bear_argument.argument:
The bull case rests on a single number — 19.0x forward P/E — that is doing an enormous amount of work while being the least reliable figure in the file. That forward multiple is derived from a consensus EPS built on +40% USD revenue growth extrapolated forward, from a street where 18 of 19 ratings are buy-or-better and zero are sells for four consecutive months. Consensus is not an independent input here; it is the same optimism being used as the justification. The genuinely observable multiple is the trailing 31.2x versus a 22.8x five-year median — a 37% premium to how the market has actually priced this asset through prior cycles. If growth normalizes toward even 20%, the 19x becomes mid-to-high 20s on a company whose own guidance concedes 2-4pp of gross margin dilution from overseas fabs. GuruFocus, scoring the business 97/100 on quality, still models fair value at $326.37 — roughly 21% below spot. The entire 31% upside to $542.64 requires the current growth-and-margin regime to be permanent, not cyclical, in the most reliably cyclical industry in technology.

The cash-flow disclosure is where the bull narrative quietly breaks. FCF of NT$992bn against net income of NT$1,698bn means only ~58% of reported earnings converts to cash — capex is eating the rest. FY2026 capex of $60-64bn, with 70-80% directed at advanced nodes and three new 3nm fabs, is not discretionary growth investment; it is the toll required to stay in the game, and it is escalating. The sentiment report explicitly names escalating advanced-node capex prompting tactical institutional rebalancing as a driver of the 08-18 selloff — institutions are reading the same capex line and reducing, not adding. A company converting 58 cents of every earnings dollar into cash, paying a 1.01% dividend, at 31x trailing, is being valued as a compounder while spending like a utility with a technology-obsolescence clock attached.

The macro and technical setup removes the cushion. The Fed held at 3.50-3.75% with a hawkish 9-3 split in which all three dissents wanted a hike, with a live FOMC on 09-15/16 and inflation still above target partly on energy — and fabs are among the most power-intensive assets on earth, so the named inflation source is also a direct cost input. With beta 1.258, any multiple compression arrives amplified. Layer on a 10% Section 122 semiconductor surcharge, Section 232 relief that is explicitly contingent and revocable, erratic US-China export licensing, Taiwan's own 279-entity watch list, and unhedgeable cross-strait tail risk with zero ADR protection. Technically, price sits below SMA-50 at 413.41 after being rejected there, RSI 71.1 is still overbought with room to unwind, the 08-18 breakdown came on above-average volume while the preceding rally to 430.97 came on volume shrinking from 9.53M to 6.29M — textbook distribution. SMA-200 at 363.53 is 12% below spot, and 479.00 has already failed once. That is not an entry point; that is the first lower high.
key_points: The 19.0x forward multiple is consensus-dependent and circular; the observable multiple is 31.2x trailing vs a 22.8x five-year median — a 37% premium — and management has already guided 2-4pp of gross margin dilution.

Earnings quality is weak: NT$992bn FCF is only ~58% of NT$1,698bn net income, and $60-64bn capex is mandatory maintenance spend, not optional growth. Institutions cited exactly this while selling on 08-18.

Unanimity is a risk factor, not a support: 19 of 19 non-sell ratings with targets 31% above spot means the thesis is fully subscribed, while GuruFocus at 97/100 quality still puts fair value 21% below spot.
Macro asymmetry with beta 1.258: a hawkish 9-3 Fed hold where all three dissents wanted a HIKE, inflation above target on energy (a direct fab input cost), and live hike risk at the 09-15/16 FOMC.

Policy and technical structure both broken: 10% Section 122 surcharge, revocable Section 232 relief, erratic China licensing, uninsurable cross-strait tail risk — against a chart rejected at SMA-50 with distribution volume and SMA-200 12% lower.
bear_argument.rebuttal_to_previous: On the sub-0.5x PEG: PEG is only meaningful if the G is durable, and the bull is annualizing a cyclical peak. Comparing a forward multiple built on peak growth against a historical median earned across full cycles is the oldest error in semiconductor investing. On Arizona: NT$36.1bn in H1 2026 versus NT$16.1bn for all of 2025 does not refute the margin thesis — one fab turning profitable says nothing about blended corporate gross margin, which is precisely what management itself guided down 2-4pp with Arizona, Kumamoto and Germany all in the plan. If the bull is right that dilution is refuted, then management is guiding wrong about its own P&L; I will take management's number. On FCF self-funding capex: it does not — FCF NT$992bn is only self-funded because capex is already deducted inside that figure, and the residual is what leaves only 58% earnings conversion. On the tariff moat: Section 232 relief is contingent on continued US expansion and revocable — that is not a moat, it is a hostage arrangement that forces perpetual high-cost domestic capex to retain a benefit the US can withdraw unilaterally, and the 10% Section 122 surcharge still applies today. On TWD: a ~6% currency move is a one-off translation effect, not earnings power, and it cuts the other way on the next reversal. On the entry point: a 410.77 stop is 0.6% below spot against ATR-14 of 13.50, meaning ordinary daily noise stops you out. And on being paid to hold the cross-strait risk: you cannot be paid for a risk you cannot size. The analysis calls it explicitly unpriceable and ADR holders have no protection — that is a binary total-loss branch, and a 19x multiple is not compensation for it.

bull_argument.argument:
The bear's case is internally consistent but it rests on a single load-bearing assumption: that +40% revenue growth on record July numbers (NT$467.58bn, +44.7% YoY) is a consensus extrapolation rather than an observed run-rate. It is observed. FY2026 is guided by management slightly above +40% in USD terms, and the July print is an actual, reported, monthly datapoint that came in above that pace. The bear cannot simultaneously say I take management's number on the 2-4pp gross-margin dilution and reject management's number on revenue. Take both: revenue up ~40%+ on a 59.9% gross margin base that becomes ~56-58% after guided dilution, against a 50.8% operating margin — still the highest-margin large-cap semiconductor P&L in existence, and 2-4pp of dilution on 40% volume growth is arithmetic that produces higher absolute gross profit, not lower. Consolidated margin percentage falls because the denominator is exploding. Arizona's NT$36.1bn in H1-26 versus NT$16.1bn for all of FY25 is proof that the incremental capacity the bear calls mandatory maintenance spend converts into profit faster than modelled.

On earnings quality: 58% FCF conversion is what a company looks like when it is building three 3nm fabs simultaneously, with 70-80% of $60-64bn going to advanced nodes. Calling that maintenance requires believing capacity added in Taiwan, Arizona and Kumamoto replaces rather than expands output — the Arizona P&L directly falsifies that. And the balance sheet forecloses the obsolescence-clock argument: debt/equity 19.9%, total debt 0.63x a single year's net income. A company with a genuine obsolescence problem shows up as rising leverage and falling returns; TSM shows 44.6% net margin and near-zero net leverage, which is why GF Score is 97/100 — the same source the bear cites for a 21%-below fair value. A trailing-anchored fair value will read 21% low against a company whose revenue is inflecting 40%+; that is a feature of the methodology, not a signal.

The technical and macro objections are timing arguments, and I will concede the timing while rejecting the thesis. Fair: 410.77 is too tight against ATR-14 of 13.50 — the correct structural stop is below 398.20, or better, below the lower Bollinger band at 384.92, which is also above the SMA-200 at 363.53. Fair also: RSI 71.1 unwinding from a rejection at SMA-50 424.79 argues for scaling in rather than a single entry, and MACD histogram still +2.00 with price above SMA-20 and SMA-200 says trend intact, not broken. On the Fed: a 9-3 hold where dissents wanted a hike is hawkish, but a hike compresses multiples across the market — it is not a TSM-specific thesis breaker. On tariffs, hostage arrangement concedes my point: TSM is the hostage the US cannot afford to shoot, and the 10% Section 122 surcharge applies to competitors who lack the reduced Section 232 treatment TSM earned. Cross-strait is unsizable and always was — which is exactly why a 40%-growth monopoly trades at 19x forward instead of 40x.
key_points: Growth is observed, not extrapolated: July 2026 revenue record NT$467.58bn +44.7% YoY, with FY2026 guided slightly above +40% by management.
2-4pp gross-margin dilution on 40%+ revenue growth raises absolute gross profit; Arizona's NT$36.1bn H1-26 vs NT$16.1bn FY25 shows new capacity converting to profit ahead of the guide.
58% FCF conversion is expansion capex, not maintenance: 70-80% of $60-64bn goes to advanced nodes across three new 3nm fabs, funded at 19.9% debt/equity with no leverage or obsolescence signature.
Valuation asymmetry stands: 18.98x forward against a 22.8x historical median and a $542.64 street target (+31%), with 18 of 19 ratings buy-or-better and zero sells for four months.

Concede the tactics, keep the thesis: use a structural stop below 384.92 rather than 410.77 (which ATR-14 13.50 guarantees is noise) and scale in while RSI 71.1 unwinds; MACD +2.00 and price above SMA-20 and SMA-200 keep the trend intact.
bull_argument.rebuttal_to_previous: On circularity: the forward multiple is anchored to management's own FY2026 guide of slightly above +40% and corroborated by an actual July print of +44.7% YoY — not to sell-side imagination. Trailing 31.2x is the multiple of a base year that the July run-rate has already left behind. On earnings quality: capex directed 70-80% to advanced nodes building three brand-new 3nm fabs is definitionally expansionary, and Arizona swinging to NT$36.1bn in one half against NT$16.1bn for all of FY25 is the receipt; a maintenance-treadmill company does not post 50.8% operating and 44.6% net margins at 0.63x net-income leverage. On unanimity: consensus with a $542.64 target and 21%-below GF Value is contradiction, not confirmation — and GF Value is a trailing-anchored method on a company mid-inflection, while GF Score 97/100 from the same vendor is the quality read that matters. On macro: a hike compresses the whole market, so it is a market-timing risk, not a thesis risk. On tariffs: revocable cuts both ways — the US revoking relief on the sole supplier of leading-edge capacity on US soil is self-harm, and the 10% Section 122 surcharge is shared industry-wide while the Section 232 exclusion is TSM-specific. On margin: I do take management's 2-4pp number — and 2-4pp off 59.9% on 40%+ volume growth is more gross profit dollars, not fewer. On self-funding: agreed it is a solvency point, restated properly as a cost-of-capital point — TSM funds the largest capex program in the industry without dilution or leverage, so equity holders capture the full earnings ramp. On the stop: fully conceded, my level was inside the noise band; the correct structural stop is below 398.20 or 384.92. On cross-strait: correct that it is unsizable — which is the reason a 40%-growth monopoly is available at 18.98x forward rather than a growth multiple. On technicals: a lower high with MACD histogram still +2.00, price above SMA-20 413.01 and SMA-200 363.53, and 08-18 volume ratio only 1.14 is profit-taking, not distribution.

bear_argument.argument:
The bull's round 2 rests on a single move repeated ten times: convert every disclosed risk into a reason the risk is not real. Take the alleged inconsistency in citing management on margin dilution while discounting management on revenue. There is no inconsistency, because the two disclosures are not symmetric in kind. July's NT$467.58bn is a backward-looking print; the 2-4pp gross margin dilution is a forward-looking commitment about the cost structure of capacity that has not yet been depreciated. I accept both at face value. What I reject is the arithmetic that follows: yes, 2-4pp off 59.9% on 40%+ volume growth grows absolute gross profit — but nobody pays 31.15x trailing earnings for absolute gross profit, they pay it for margin trajectory, and the direction of that trajectory is the thing management just told you turns negative. At 18.98x forward the market is already paying for the +40% year. The bull's own framing concedes this: growth is observed, therefore it is in the tape, therefore it is in the price. The 13.69% gap to the 52w high is not the market failing to notice a record July; the market saw the record July and sold it on 08-18. That is what a fully-discounted print looks like.

On earnings quality the bull inverts the burden of proof. 58% conversion is expansion capex, not maintenance is a hypothesis, not a finding — the only thing observable is that NT$706bn of reported income did not become cash, that $60-64bn of capex is 70-80% concentrated in the single most expensive node transition ever attempted, and that three greenfield 3nm fabs are being built simultaneously across three jurisdictions with three different labor, power, and permitting cost bases. The claim that 50.8% operating margin at 0.63x leverage disproves a treadmill gets the sequencing wrong: the treadmill is visible in the capex line first and the margin line second, which is precisely why management guided the margin down and precisely why the current margin cannot be used as evidence against it. Arizona's NT$36.1bn is the weakest exhibit in the bull case, not the strongest — a single fab's H1 P&L, at a site enjoying a Section 232 exclusion that both sides agree is revocable, tells you nothing about blended margin across a fleet where Kumamoto and the two other 3nm ramps are simultaneously pre-profitable. And the GF Value dismissal is unfalsifiable by construction: the vendor's 97/100 quality score is accepted, the same vendor's $326.37 fair value 21% below spot is a methodology artifact. Pick one epistemology.

The macro and structural rebuttals are where the bull's discipline breaks down most visibly. Calling a Fed hike market-timing risk, not thesis risk is a category error when the thesis is a 31x trailing multiple on a beta-1.258 name — multiple compression IS the thesis risk for a stock whose entire bull case is a valuation re-rating toward $542.64. Three dissenters voting for a hike, with inflation running above 2% partly on energy in a business that is structurally power-intensive, is a double hit: discount rate up, input cost up. Beta is symmetric is true and irrelevant — symmetry around 09-15/16 is a coin flip, not an edge. On Section 232, revoking it would be self-harm assumes a counterparty that optimizes for its own economic interest, which the H200 sequence (banned, unbanned, then a 25% tariff) directly falsifies within the same dataset. And the most dangerous sentence in the bull case is that cross-strait risk earns you a valuation discount: 18.98x forward on 40% growth is not a discount — it is what consensus produces when 18 of 19 analysts are already positioned. You are not being compensated for the tail.
key_points: The observed/extrapolated distinction cuts against the bull: a record July that the market sold on 08-18, leaving price 13.69% below the 52w high, is a print already in the price — while the 2-4pp dilution guide is the only forward disclosure and it points down.

Absolute gross profit growth is the wrong metric for a 31.15x trailing multiple; multiples are paid on margin trajectory, and management just guided the trajectory negative across three simultaneous greenfield 3nm ramps.

Arizona's NT$36.1bn is one fab, one half-year, at the one site holding a revocable Section 232 exclusion — not evidence about blended fleet margin, and it cannot rebut a guide management issued with Arizona's numbers already in hand.
Selective vendor trust: GF Score 97/100 is accepted as signal while the same vendor's $326.37 fair value (21% below spot) is dismissed as artifact.

Multiple compression is not market-timing noise for a 31x/beta-1.258 name whose bull case IS a re-rate to $542.64 — a 9-3 hawkish hold with all three dissents wanting a HIKE, plus energy-driven inflation into power-intensive fabs, hits discount rate and cost base simultaneously.

18.98x forward with 18 of 19 buys and zero sells for four months is not payment for cross-strait tail risk — it is the output of a crowded consensus, so the tail is uncompensated rather than discounted.
bear_argument.rebuttal_to_previous: The bull concedes the stop was inside the noise band and that RSI 71.1 into an SMA-50 rejection argues against a single entry, then treats the fix as mechanical: move the stop to 398.20 or 384.92 and scale in. But widening the stop to 384.92 is accepting a 6.9% structural drawdown on a name whose ATR-14 is 13.50, which means the correct stop is roughly 2 ATRs away and the wrong one was under 0.2 — the honest reading is that this chart has no defensible stop at current price, only a choice of how much you are willing to lose. Advancing on shrinking volume and declining on above-average volume is the textbook signature of supply overhanging demand, and it is why 419.63/424.79/430.97 now sit as a stacked resistance shelf rather than a base. On the substantive rebuttals: the you-cannot-cite-management-selectively charge collapses because I cite both — the record revenue and the margin guide — and note only that the market has already paid for one and not yet for the other. The asymmetric treatment of the same vendor's two outputs is the clearest tell in the bull case. Labelling the central risk exogenous mislabels it when a re-rate to $542.64 IS a multiple-expansion bet placed directly into a hawkish Fed. And the self-harm assumption about US policy is refuted by the H200 sequence sitting in the same dataset.
